today_focus.title: Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a min
today_focus.brief: Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a min。它反映的是一线 builder 对产品和工作流变化的即时反馈，价值在于捕捉正式新闻之前的使用趋势。
today_focus.social_original_text:
Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a minimum reinvesting efficiency savings back into the business in new areas (sales, marketing, etc.).

David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs, articulated this perfectly in a NYTimes OpEd last week. The AI boom is both creating all new jobs in the build out of AI systems and the implementation across sectors, but also freeing up dollars to invest in areas that have been underfunded or have more demand now because of AI.

Most businesses have been constrained by how much software they can produce at a given cost, how many sales reps they can hire, how many marketing campaigns they can run, how they can do outbound customer success motions with enough tailoring, how they can find more risk in their business and prevent it, and 100s of other things.

When AI makes it possible to do more of this, investment goes back into the business. The companies that better serve their customers win over the long run, and those that just try and find savings end up doing worse.

industry_views.social_original_text:
Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a minimum reinvesting efficiency savings back into the business in new areas (sales, marketing, etc.).

David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs, articulated this perfectly in a NYTimes OpEd last week. The AI boom is both creating all new jobs in the build out of AI systems and the implementation across sectors, but also freeing up dollars to invest in areas that have been underfunded or have more demand now because of AI.

Most businesses have been constrained by how much software they can produce at a given cost, how many sales reps they can hire, how many marketing campaigns they can run, how they can do outbound customer success motions with enough tailoring, how they can find more risk in their business and prevent it, and 100s of other things.

When AI makes it possible to do more of this, investment goes back into the business. The companies that better serve their customers win over the long run, and those that just try and find savings end up doing worse.

items.title: 乘客蓝牙设备名称触发安全警报，美联航客机起飞 1 小时后被迫返航
items.brief: 乘客蓝牙设备名称触发安全警报，美联航客机起飞 1 小时后被迫返航。这类变化会改写上线边界，适合放进产品发布前的风险检查。
evidence_titles: 乘客蓝牙设备名称触发安全警报，美联航客机起飞 1 小时后被迫返航
evidence_summaries: IT之家 6 月 1 日消息，据 TheVerge 报道，当地时间周六晚间，美国联合航空一架从纽瓦克飞往马略卡岛帕尔马的 236 号航班，起飞仅一小时后便因一则蓝牙信号引发的安全隐患被迫返航。多名自称搭乘该航班的 Reddit 用户表示，机组人员多次要求乘客关闭蓝牙设备。一名网友称，机组还给出了一分钟限时提醒，告知机上仍有两台设备的蓝牙处于开启状态。 IT之家注意到，有网友提到，空乘人员当时说道：“这种恶作剧害得所有人都受牵连。” 一段空中交通管制存档录音证实，事件起因是一台可被搜索到的蓝牙音箱的设备名称。录音中提到：“安保人员已到场。有人使用的蓝牙音箱，设备名是一个四字粗俗词汇。因此整架飞机包括货舱都需要接受检查，机上乘客也必须撤离。” 虽然录音并未直接证实该蓝牙设备名是“炸弹”一词的外界猜测，但结合机组人员与地面安保的处置行动来看，这一推测合乎情理。此事也给大家提了个醒：别自以为把无线网络或蓝牙设备取名搞怪很有趣，这类行为往往会引发不必要的麻烦。
items.memory_note: 判断：非AI原生事件，但精准映射大模型上线前的“长尾安全边界”盲区。关注点：LLM产品常依赖RLHF对齐常规分布，却缺乏对极端语义触发器的鲁棒性设计。航空级安全协议启示我们，AI部署需从“能力优先”转向“失效安全优先”，建立类似红蓝对抗的边界压力测试，而非仅依赖基准测试刷榜。
reading_questions: 当前LLM安全对齐（RLHF/DPO）能否覆盖此类非典型语义触发？
AI产品如何平衡“用户体验”与“航空级安全冗余”？

items.title: Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a min
items.brief: Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a min。它反映的是一线 builder 对产品和工作流变化的即时反馈，价值在于捕捉正式新闻之前的使用趋势。
items.social_original_text:
Again, maybe counterintuitive, but in the majority of conversations I have with CIOs, CTOs, and CEOs in large enterprises, they are either growing due to AI (in new job functions like FDEs, engineering, etc.) or at a minimum reinvesting efficiency savings back into the business in new areas (sales, marketing, etc.).

David Solomon, CEO of Goldman Sachs, articulated this perfectly in a NYTimes OpEd last week. The AI boom is both creating all new jobs in the build out of AI systems and the implementation across sectors, but also freeing up dollars to invest in areas that have been underfunded or have more demand now because of AI.

Most businesses have been constrained by how much software they can produce at a given cost, how many sales reps they can hire, how many marketing campaigns they can run, how they can do outbound customer success motions with enough tailoring, how they can find more risk in their business and prevent it, and 100s of other things.

When AI makes it possible to do more of this, investment goes back into the business. The companies that better serve their customers win over the long run, and those that just try and find savings end up doing worse.
items.translation_zh: 这听起来可能有些反直觉，但在与大型企业 CIO、CTO 和 CEO 的大多数交流中，他们要么正因 AI 而扩张（新增 FDEs、工程等新岗位），要么至少将效率提升节省下来的资金重新投入到业务的新领域（如销售、营销等）。 高盛 CEO David Solomon 上周在《纽约时报》评论文章中对此做了完美阐述。AI 热潮不仅在 AI 系统建设和跨行业落地中创造了大量全新岗位，还释放了资金，用于投资那些过去资金不足或因 AI 而需求激增的领域。 过去，大多数企业都受限于诸多瓶颈：在既定成本下能开发多少软件、能雇佣多少销售代表、能开展多少营销活动、如何进行足够定制化的主动客户成功运营、如何识别并防范业务风险，以及数百项其他事务。 当 AI 让企业有能力在这些方面做得更多时，投资将重新注入业务。长期来看，能更好服务客户的企业将赢得胜利，而那些仅仅试图削减成本的企业最终反而会表现更差。
